findings: Use CRDTs (e.g. Yjs/Automerge-style RGA or Peritext for rich text) rather than centralized Operational Transformation, because CRDTs guarantee mathematically that concurrent edits converge without a single serializing authority, which is what makes zero-data-loss merging survive a regional outage instead of just a network blip.

Give every client a local-first CRDT replica so keystrokes apply to local state immediately and render before any network round trip; this is what actually delivers sub-200ms perceived latency, since it decouples perceived responsiveness from server RTT entirely rather than trying to make the network itself faster.

Data residency is enforced by regional data domiciling, not application-level filtering: each tenant is assigned a home region (US or EU) at provisioning time, and that tenant's document content, CRDT operation log, and audit log are stored and processed exclusively on infrastructure physically located in that region.

A global anycast/GeoDNS edge layer terminates client connections near the user but immediately proxies the collaboration session to the document's home-region collab cluster (determined by document/tenant metadata, not by requesting user's location), so an EU document's content and compute never cross into US infrastructure even when a US-based collaborator joins it.

For documents shared across US and EU collaborators, the non-home-region users deliberately absorb extra round-trip latency to the document's home region rather than the architecture replicating or caching plaintext content outside its residency zone — sovereignty is treated as the non-negotiable constraint and latency for that minority case is the accepted tradeoff.

Regional collaboration servers are relay/persistence nodes, not merge arbiters: they append incoming CRDT updates to a durable per-document operation log and fan them out to other connected clients, while the actual conflict-free merge happens independently on each replica — this keeps the server simple and avoids making it a single point of correctness failure.

Document state is persisted as periodic CRDT snapshots plus an append-only operation log (not a mutable 'current document' row), enabling compaction, exact replay for debugging/audit correlation, and recovery to any point without reconstructing merge history from scratch.

The audit log requirement ('never lose an event, even across a regional outage') is in tension with EU residency, since a naive fix would replicate audit events to another region; resolve this by keeping the audit log itself region-pinned too, and instead achieving outage resilience via multi-AZ synchronous replication and a durable broker (e.g. Kafka/Kinesis-equivalent with 3+ AZ acks) within the same region, so a single-AZ or zonal failure never loses events while data never leaves the EU boundary.

True whole-region-loss durability for the audit log (not just an AZ) requires a second region within the same jurisdiction (e.g. eu-west + eu-central) used for active-passive or active-active audit log replication, rather than replicating into the US — this satisfies 'never loses an event across a regional outage' without violating the hard EU residency requirement, and is called out explicitly as the only way to reconcile those two constraints.

Clients buffer unacknowledged edits and audit events in durable local storage (IndexedDB/disk) and retry with idempotent, uniquely-IDed operations until the regional service acknowledges persistence, so a transient regional outage causes a client-visible retry/reconnect rather than silent data loss, and duplicate delivery on retry doesn't double-count because audit events are deduplicated by ID.

The audit log is architecturally separate from the document content store (distinct append-only, tamper-evident/hash-chained log) even though both are region-pinned together, so compliance auditing, retention, and immutability guarantees can be reasoned about and tested independently of the collaborative-editing data path.

Presence and ephemeral collaboration metadata (live cursors, who's online, typing indicators) are treated as a separate, non-durable, region-local pub/sub channel that is allowed to be lossy — since losing a cursor position has no compliance or correctness consequence, it isn't burdened with the same durability machinery as content edits and audit events, keeping that hot path cheap and fast.

For latency-sensitive intra-region collaboration (the common case: EU users on EU documents, US users on US documents), the whole path — edge termination, collab server, and storage — is kept within one region/metro so the sub-200ms budget is spent on local network hops and CRDT-merge/broadcast overhead, not cross-continent transit.

Regional database choice favors either a region-scoped conventional store (e.g. per-region Postgres/object storage with intra-region multi-AZ replicas) for operational simplicity, or, as an alternative for organizations wanting one logical global control plane, a geo-partitioned distributed database (e.g. CockroachDB-style row/range domiciling) that enforces residency at the storage layer itself rather than relying purely on deployment topology — flagged as a build-vs-operate tradeoff rather than a single mandated answer.

Chaos/failover testing of a full regional outage (not just node failure) is called out as a required verification step, since the 'never lose an audit event across a regional outage' requirement is a claim about behavior under a failure mode that unit tests won't exercise — it needs to be proven by actually killing a region in a staging environment and confirming buffered client retries and cross-AZ/cross-region audit replication recover cleanly.
